sections.h2: How a deed gets recorded in Lake County
sections.html:
It takes two counters in Painesville. The Transfer Office (the Auditor's first floor) comes first, where you complete an Exempt Form or a Conveyance Fee Form and get the deed stamped. The Recorder, on the lower level of the Administration Building, comes second and processes the deed on the spot.

The Recorder is at 105 Main Street, Lower Level, with P.O. Box 490, Painesville, OH 44077, phone (440) 350-2510 and email recorder@lakecountyohio.gov. Counter service runs weekdays from 8 a.m. until 4 p.m., closed on holidays, and the last recordings of the day should be in before 3:45.

A mailed filing has its own checklist. Each auditor and engineer stamp has to be on the deed already, and the envelope needs a cover letter, one check for the Recorder, one for the Auditor and a stamped return envelope. If the Auditor's stamp is missing, the deed comes back rejected.

The Recorder bills $34.00 for a two page deed and $5.00 for preservation, and each page past the second adds $8.00. The Auditor collects its own transfer charges, which is why the office wants two checks.

Lake County deed charges
ChargeAmountPayee
Deed up to two pages$34.00 plus a $5.00 preservation feeRecorder
Each page after two$8.00Recorder
Reference to an earlier recorded document$4.00 apieceRecorder
Nonconforming document$20.00 penaltyRecorder
Conveyance fee$4.00 per $1,000 of valueAuditor
Transfer fee$0.50 for each parcelAuditor

The $4.00 breaks into a $1.00 state share and a $3.00 county share. The county piece was set by a commissioners' resolution dated March 26, 1990 under section 322.02.

sections.h2: Paperwork the Auditor wants with a transfer
sections.html:
Either side of the deal, or a representative, may hand in the deed, and mail is accepted. Everything must be complete, signed and notarized. The Transfer Office takes transfers between 8 and 4.

  • A DTE 100 or DTE 100EX goes with every transfer.
  • Parcels in the homestead or CAUV farm programs need a notarized DTE 101 or DTE 102 first.
  • A sale of anything short of a whole platted sublot, such as a piece of a sublot or a metes and bounds tract, must clear the Tax Map Department. Exempt transfers skip that stop.
  • Taking someone off a deed means drafting a new deed, so call a title company or attorney.

The county posts owner names exactly as the recorded deed spells them, so a typo on the deed travels into the tax records.

sections.h2: Transfers exempt from the conveyance fee
sections.html:
Section 319.54(G)(3) holds the exemption list, and the reason is written on the form that section 319.202 requires. Examples that fit house sales:

  • A deed given only as security for a debt, or releasing that security.
  • A sale for delinquent taxes or assessments.
  • Survivorship transfers under sections 5302.17 or 5302.18.
  • A deed to a trustee when the maker kept an unlimited power to revoke.
  • A transfer to a non-dealer who is only a stop on the way to a prompt resale.

One shortcut: a Transfer on Death Beneficiary Designation Affidavit skips the Auditor and goes straight to the Recorder, with the recording fee and a return envelope.

A deed can be e-recorded through four partners: Corporation Service Company, eRecording Partners Network, Simplifile and Hop Docs. You deal with one of those firms, because the Recorder's office does not operate the portal itself.

For research, the AVA search engine gives basic results and Laredo Select goes deeper, but it needs a registered account. Filings cannot carry watermarks. The office's services menu also lists a property fraud alert and a video chat on that topic.

The Recorder's guidelines restate section 317.114. A deed outside them is still accepted but costs the $20.00 penalty. Before signing, confirm:

  • Type at 10 point or bigger, on paper cut between 8.5 by 11 and 8.5 by 14.
  • Black or blue ink, with nothing highlighted.
  • One inch margins at the sides and foot, three inches clear at the top of page one for stamps, and an inch and a half on the pages after.
  • A title, a date, typed names and titles under every signature, and a notary block that shows the commission expiration.
  • The preparer's name and a full legal description.

When one document refers to an earlier one, cite its number, or its book and page, along with the recording date. Each such reference adds $4.00.

Lake County had 232,217 residents in mid 2025 and 107,571 housing units. The ownership rate is 75.8 percent, median value of owned homes is $214,100, median gross rent is $1,113 and median household income is $80,925. School district names carry weight in listings: Mentor Public, Painesville City Local, Willoughby-Eastlake City, Wickliffe City, Kirtland Local, Madison Local, Perry Local, Riverside Local and Fairport Harbor Exempted Village each cover part of the county.

sections.h2: Tax questions at a Lake County closing
sections.html:
Real estate taxes for 2026, payable in 2027, are due February 24 and July 21, 2027, and bills mail out in mid-January and mid-June. A buyer's lender or the title company will ask for the status of those halves, so request the Treasurer's payoff before the closing date. The Treasurer's billing line is (440) 350-2516, and the Auditor's real estate staff answer address and credit questions at (440) 350-2532.

If a record shows a wrong owner address, the Auditor corrects owner addresses while the Treasurer handles the tax mailing address, so changes may need two calls.

Gather the signed, notarized deed and any exemption or value form before you leave home. Stop at the Transfer Office first, pay the conveyance and transfer fees and get the stamp. Walk the stamped deed down to the Recorder and pay its charges with a separate check. If the parcel is only part of a sublot, visit the Tax Map Department before the Auditor. Leave time before 3:45 so the deed is recorded the same day, and keep the receipts for your closing file. If your lender is paying off a mortgage, ask your title company to confirm that the release was filed, since it is a separate recording at the same counter. A buyer who plans to use a transfer on death designation should skip the Auditor and file straight with the Recorder.

faqs.q: Where is the Lake County Recorder's office?
faqs.a: Lower Level, 105 Main Street, Painesville, OH 44077, with mail going to P.O. Box 490. The number is (440) 350-2510 and counter hours run weekdays from 8 to 4, closed on holidays.

faqs.q: What is the Lake County conveyance fee?
faqs.a: $4.00 per $1,000 of the purchase price plus $0.50 per parcel. It is paid to the Auditor before the Recorder sees the deed.

faqs.q: Do I need two checks to record a deed in Lake County?
faqs.a: Yes. The guidelines want a check for each office, one made out to the Lake County Recorder and one to the Lake County Auditor. Mailed filings also need a stamped self-addressed envelope, or the originals come back collect on delivery.

faqs.q: When does a Lake County sale need Tax Map approval?
faqs.a: When money changes hands and the parcel is anything other than a full sublot in a platted subdivision. Part of a sublot and metes and bounds tracts both qualify. Exempt transfers do not need it.

faqs.q: Can I mail a deed to the Lake County Auditor?
faqs.a: Yes, mail transfers are accepted. Address them to the Auditor's Real Estate Transfer Office, 105 Main Street, PO Box 490, Painesville, OH 44077. The deed is passed to the Recorder after transfer.
